props.title: lev <noun> <verb>, one owner per word
props.subtitle: 4 informed reviewers + 4 clean-blind guesses. 3-1 to extend the rule we already have. 14 choices left for you.

props.content:
- **Panel:** 3 Opus lenses (ontology, operator/agent UX, canon fit) + Fable 5.1, all on the identical prompt, deep-scanning the repo. Plus 4 clean-blind guesses from a one-paragraph description. The first 3 blind runs leaked repo knowledge and are excluded.
- **Census:** 181 root words from 209 claims; 19 words have several claimants (`status` has 7); the winner is picked by load order.
- **Verdict:** RECLASSIFY 3 · SHIP 1 (Fable). Everyone agrees on the grammar; they differ on where the word list lives.
- **Checked by me:** `lev workstream list --json` returns `operation.id: "workstream.workstream"` — the verb is dropped today (two reviewers claimed otherwise).
- **Found on the way (no decision needed):** unknown root words hang instead of failing fast; `lev --output=toon projects list` is read as an unknown command.
- **Raw record:** `~/.local/state/lev/tribunal/n1-namespace-ontology-20260926/`.

items.title: Extend the rule we have, or author a list of root words?
items.insight: **3 of 4 informed reviewers: RECLASSIFY.** The ontology already exists (`dna/fractal.yaml:127-148`, "Domain = module"); only the CLI flattens it by load order. **Fable 5.1: SHIP**, but with an authored word registry.
items.detail:
- Evidence all 4 share: 19 words with more than one claimant, 44 unrunnable roots, first-writer-wins at `core/poly/src/registry/commands.ts:200,231`.
- Majority: poly **derives** the registry from folders + `dna/entities.yaml`, and fails the build on a collision. An authored list would be "split-brain against poly.dna.yaml:74 registry_is_derived" (ontology reviewer).
- Fable: author word→owner in `dna/standards/source-namespaces.yaml#roots` and amend fractal.yaml:138 to "Domain = registered root". That file already gives `status` to `@lev-os/config` (a storage route), which collides with a poly-owned `lev status`.
- Caveat from the comparison: the split follows model family exactly (all Opus RECLASSIFY, Fable SHIP), so the majority is less independent than 3 votes suggest.

options.label: Extend the existing rule
options.desc: Enforce fractal domain addressing in poly, add dna/entities.yaml as the second noun class, a closed poly verb list, and `lev status` as a follow-on slice

options.label: Authored root-word registry
options.desc: Fable's version: source-namespaces.yaml#roots lists every root word and its owner; fractal.yaml:138 is amended

items.title: May a module's own name act as a root verb? (lev exec, lev now)
items.insight: You said "root word is my verb needs to be allowed" and "i also dont want lev exec exec". **All 4 clean-blind reviewers expected no module-named verbs** at the root.
items.detail:
- Against: "Executing belongs to `lev flow run`" (ontology, blind); host verbs are "the only commands without a noun" (canon-fit, blind); "A module can never own a root verb" (canon-fit, informed).
- For: operator-ux (informed) keeps `lev exec "<task>"` as the default capability of the exec noun; ontology (informed) likewise.
- The lint rule this confirms: an owner-verb must equal the module name, and `lev exec exec` is an error.

options.label: Yes — only the module's own name
options.desc: `lev exec`, `lev now` run the module's default capability; nothing else may act as a bare verb

options.label: No — always lev <noun> <verb>
options.desc: Match the blind expectation: `lev exec run`, `lev now render`

items.title: Which root verbs take no noun and belong to poly?
items.insight: All 8 seats want a **small closed set** that includes status, doctor, help and version. They differ on the rest.
items.detail:
- ontology adds init, install, find, up/down/ps.
- operator-ux adds init, install, upgrade (at most 8).
- canon-fit adds search and validate as fan-in across nouns.
- Fable adds exec, find, search, work, up, down, ps, routing.

options.label: status, doctor, help, version
options.desc: The four every seat agrees on; everything else nests under a noun

options.label: + init, install, upgrade
options.desc: Add the setup words (from core/build)

options.label: + search, validate, find
options.desc: Add fan-in verbs that gather from every noun

options.label: Fable's wide list
options.desc: + exec, find, search, work, up, down, ps, routing

items.title: May a root verb simply forward to one module? (find → index find, work → sdlc work)
items.insight: If yes, a module gets a root verb that is not its own name — the lint's owner-verb rule is bypassed. If no, `find`, `search` and `work` lose their roots.
items.detail:
- Forwarding examples proposed: find→index.find, search→research.search, work→sdlc.work, up→daemon.start, upgrade→build.upgrade.
- Under the no-shims canon (migrations are delete-and-replace), forwards would be permanent parts of the grammar, not migration aliases.

options.label: No — root verbs are fan-outs or poly's own
options.desc: Module verbs stay nested: `lev index find`, `lev sdlc work`

options.label: Yes — a poly-owned forward list
options.desc: Each forward declared once in dna/core/poly.dna.yaml

items.title: Can a module claim a noun that is not its folder name?
items.insight: This decides `lev graph` vs `lev context-graph`, and whether `lev task` belongs to orchestration.
items.detail:
- No: ontology, operator-ux (informed); canon-fit (blind): "config.yaml declares verbs ... never the noun".
- Yes: canon-fit (informed) `poly.nouns: [graph]` on context-graph, `[task, cdo]` on orchestration — its own risk list calls this a "noun land-grab".
- Entity nouns (task, session, decision…) still come from dna/entities.yaml either way.

options.label: No — noun = folder name
options.desc: Entity nouns come only from dna/entities.yaml, each with one owner

options.label: Yes — declared in config.yaml
options.desc: Modules list extra nouns under poly.nouns; the compiler rejects duplicates

items.title: What counts as a stutter?
items.insight: Canon: "a segment never restates an ancestor's word" (`dna/fractal.yaml:139`).
items.detail:
- Literal repeat: `lev exec exec`.
- Same stem: `lev validator validate` — operator-ux proposed it; Fable calls it "the validator/validate stutter that fractal.yaml:139 forbids".

options.label: Repeat or same stem
options.desc: Both `lev exec exec` and `lev validator validate` fail the lint

options.label: Literal repeat only
options.desc: Only an identical word is an error

items.title: Turning the lint on
items.insight: Failing closed today breaks the build: 19 words already have two or more claimants.
items.detail:
- Ratchet: record today's collisions; new ones fail; the list can only shrink.
- Fable warns a date-expiring quarantine list "is itself a thing that can be forgotten".
- operator-ux wants "FAILS CLOSED on any overlap" with no list.

options.label: Shrinking baseline
options.desc: Record today's 19; any new collision fails; entries are removed as nouns move

options.label: Baseline with expiry dates
options.desc: Each entry must be resolved by a date

options.label: Fail closed now
options.desc: Fix all 19 before the lint lands

items.title: What should lev status read?
items.insight: **All 8 seats:** status ≠ doctor, one versioned JSON on every surface, a sessions block, a needs-you block, and a deterministic `next` list. They differ on speed vs freshness.
items.detail:
- Clean-blind reviewers expect a fast local read with no daemon.
- The ontology reviewer's live task scan took over 120 s; Fable found 5 of 13 sources degraded.
- `core/config` already declares a `status.read_model` route that nothing uses (Fable).

options.label: Snapshot + --deep
options.desc: Read a precomputed snapshot; `--deep` rescans live with per-source time limits

options.label: Always live
options.desc: Fan out to every noun each time, each under a time limit

items.title: Should lev status ever exit non-zero?
items.insight: Blind reviewers expect a `--check` flag that fails on bad health. Informed reviewers forbid any verdict outside core/eval.
items.detail:
- "status reports and never fails on findings" (ontology, blind).
- "next[] must stay a deterministic rule projection; the moment an LLM ranks it, lev status becomes a verdict surface outside core/eval" (Fable).

options.label: Never — doctor fails, status observes
options.desc: `lev status` always exits 0 on findings; `lev doctor` owns failure

options.label: Allow --check
options.desc: A threshold on observations, not a verdict

items.title: Who owns lev search? (you earlier picked research, then said "see above")
items.insight: The 4 informed reviewers hold 4 positions. **All clean-blind reviewers expect one root search across everything.**
items.detail:
- Today root `lev search` resolves to knowledge-registry, which returns not_implemented.
- ontology: no root. operator-ux: alias to research if your pick stands. canon-fit: root fan-in, local index by default. Fable: alias to research.search.

options.label: Root search across all nouns
options.desc: Poly fans out; the local index answers by default; `--web` routes to research

options.label: Research owns it
options.desc: `lev search` = `lev research search` (your earlier pick)

options.label: No root search
options.desc: Only `lev index find`, `lev research search`

items.title: How do entities change state?
items.insight: You asked for CRUD that feels "rote/mechanical". One verb for every entity is the most rote.
items.detail:
- ontology, operator-ux (informed): `lev <type> move <id> <state>`, checked against the type's lifecycle.
- All clean-blind: named transitions (`task start`, `task done`), and `update --state` refused.
- canon-fit: close / link / supersede.

options.label: One verb: move <id> <state>
options.desc: Same for every entity type; the type's lifecycle rejects illegal moves

options.label: Named transitions per type
options.desc: `lev task start`, `lev decision rule` — declared per type

options.label: close / link / supersede
options.desc: canon-fit's set

items.title: What does delete mean for an entity?
items.insight: All 8 seats agree: **never an rm by default**, and execution records stay append-only. Only the verb name differs.
items.detail: - archive (ontology, operator-ux); close/supersede (canon-fit); delete as a move to archived (Fable); delete + restore (all clean-blind).

options.label: delete = soft, plus restore
options.desc: CRUD word; moves to archived; `restore` brings it back; `--purge` is explicit

options.label: archive
options.desc: No delete verb at all

items.title: Who gets the word "claim"?
items.insight: Every clean-blind reviewer means a **lock with a time limit** on a task. In the repo, a Claim is a **proof submission** (`.lev/claims`, `core/exec` done handler).
items.detail:
- Three informed reviewers propose `lev exec claim` for proof submission.
- The lock already has vocabulary: `work assign / start / release` (`dna/vernacular.yaml:1006`).

options.label: Claim stays proof submission
options.desc: The time-limited lock is `lev work assign/release`

options.label: Claim becomes the lock
options.desc: Rename proof submission to something else

items.title: Five nouns without a clear owner: session, task, work, vault, graph
items.insight: The reviewers name candidates but agree these need **your ruling**, one by one.
items.detail:
- session: core/workstream (operator-ux) or core/substrate (Fable).
- task: workstream CRUD (Fable), orchestration (canon-fit), sdlc packet (operator-ux).
- work: sdlc (runtime today) or core/workstream (vernacular).
- vault: plugins/vault (see the M1 page).
- graph: context-graph owns data ops; exec keeps proof submission.

options.label: Separate page, one card each
options.desc: I build a follow-up page after these rulings

options.label: Take the reviewers' leading picks
options.desc: session→workstream, task→workstream, work→sdlc, vault→plugins/vault, graph→context-graph
